hints: Look carefully at W, X, Y and Z and ask which two pressure lines are crossing at each point, ventricular with atrial or ventricular with aortic.
Remember valves open when pressure behind them is higher and close when pressure in front is higher, so AV valves respond to ventricle vs atrium and semilunar valves respond to ventricle vs aorta.
walkthrough:
**Recall the golden rule for valves**

Think like blood. Blood always flows from high pressure to low pressure. A valve opens when pressure behind it becomes greater, and it slams shut when pressure in front becomes greater to stop backflow.

**Sort out W and Z using ventricle vs atrium**

W is at about 0.18 s when ventricular pressure (solid line) starts to rise above atrial pressure (dotted line) at the start of ventricular systole. This pushes the atrioventricular valves shut. Z is at about 0.47 s when ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure during diastole, so the atrioventricular valves open to let the ventricle fill.

**Sort out X and Y using ventricle vs aorta**

X is at about 0.2 s when ventricular pressure (solid) rises above aortic pressure (dashed) so the semilunar valves are forced open and blood is ejected. Y is at about 0.45 s when ventricular pressure falls below aortic pressure, so the semilunar valves close to prevent backflow from aorta to ventricle.

So the pattern is:
$$W = closes, X = opens, Y = closes, Z = opens$$

options.A: W is wrong. W is AV valves closing, not opening, because ventricular pressure is rising above atrial pressure.
options.B: W is wrong. W cannot be opens, ventricular contraction closes AV valves to stop backflow into the atrium.
options.C: Exactly right. W closes AV valves, X opens semilunar valves, Y closes semilunar valves, Z opens AV valves.
options.D: X and Y are wrong. X is semilunar opening not closing, and Y is semilunar closing not opening.
